WHY_THE_AUDIT_FAILED_AND_WHAT_THAT_DOES_.cause: experiments/run_state.py:373 calls check_block(min(want), max(want), plan.seed_class) WITHOUT an experiment_id, so the audit sees this run's own Rule-9 registry reservation (ROUTED_COMPOSITION_OUTCOME_V1, 20200001..20200064) as a foreign overlap. check_block already accepts experiment_id; the audit never passes it, and AuditPlan has no field to carry it.
WHY_THE_AUDIT_FAILED_AND_WHAT_THAT_DOES_.consequence_beyond_this_run: Any experiment that follows Rule 9 (allocate the block BEFORE spending seeds) will fail its own seal. This is the first run to go through seal(), and it exposed the defect. It is a latent defect in the shared integrity gate, not in this experiment.
WHY_THE_AUDIT_FAILED_AND_WHAT_THAT_DOES_.why_my_pre_launch_checks_missed_it: The synthetic dry-run of run_audit passed because the seed block was NOT yet allocated in the registry at that point, so the overlap never arose. I had read the audit's claim-derivation logic but not its seed_class branch. C11 passed experiment_id correctly, so the contract stage could not see it either.
WHY_THE_AUDIT_FAILED_AND_WHAT_THAT_DOES_.what_it_does_not_mean: The other 12 gating checks passed: spec_frozen, rows_present, row_count (384), cell_seed_block_exact (6 cells, 0 offending), no_duplicate_seeds, pairing_valid, binary blue_win and draw, derived blue_win and draw (0 disagreements in 384 rows), and BOTH primary claims re-derived from the persisted rows at 0.00e+00 absolute difference. The failure is a registry self-overlap, not a data-integrity finding.
WHY_THE_AUDIT_FAILED_AND_WHAT_THAT_DOES_.what_it_does_mean: The record is AUDIT_FAILED and must be quoted as such. The re-derivation agreeing exactly is strong evidence the numbers are internally consistent; it is not the same thing as a sealed record.
WHY_THE_AUDIT_FAILED_AND_WHAT_THAT_DOES_.sanctioned_path_not_taken_by_this_agent: The state machine's own message says to freeze the failed state and start a NEW label rather than overwrite a recorded outcome. That means fixing the audit to pass experiment_id (with tests) and re-auditing the SAME persisted rows under a new label: no new episodes, no new seeds. That edits shared integrity infrastructure after the verdict is known, so it is left as a PI decision.

PRIMARY_GATES_RECOMPUTED_FROM_PERSISTED_.frozen_meaning: The router helps B but breaks the Pole-A guardrail. Not a promotion.
PRIMARY_GATES_RECOMPUTED_FROM_PERSISTED_.not_underpowered: The spec said to report underpowered preservation if A is merely noisy at n=64. It is not merely noisy: the harm's LCB95 is +0.047, so the interval excludes zero. The router is demonstrably harmful to Pole A, not just unproven safe. Both split halves agree in sign and size.

INTEGRITY_CHECKED_INDEPENDENTLY_OF_THE_A.check: STATE_B_TRIGGER episodes whose router never triggered must equal FIXED_2A2D exactly, if the arms differ only in the composition sequence.
INTEGRITY_CHECKED_INDEPENDENTLY_OF_THE_A.result: Pole A: 25 untriggered STATE episodes, 25 of 25 bit-identical to FIXED_2A2D on blue_score, red_score, steps and blue_win.
INTEGRITY_CHECKED_INDEPENDENTLY_OF_THE_A.limit_stated: Pole B had ZERO untriggered episodes (64 of 64 triggered), so this check verifies nothing about Pole B. The Pole-B arm identity rests on C5 (pinned-vs-fixed parity) and C8 (anchor to the sealed oracle rows) from the contract stage.
INTEGRITY_CHECKED_INDEPENDENTLY_OF_THE_A.derivation_cross_check: Ticks in 4A_0D were recovered from the CSV as (attack_ticks - 2*steps)/2. The resulting tick fractions (A 0.1094, B 0.7674) match the executor's independently recorded telemetry (A 0.109375, B 0.767383).

B_capture.reading: The denominator interval excludes zero, so the ratio is reportable under the spec's rule. It exceeds 1: on Pole B the router did better than fixed 4A/0D, so 4A/0D is not a ceiling and 'fraction captured' is the wrong frame for B.

A_damage_avoided.reading: Reportable (denominator excludes zero) but very imprecise: the numerator interval spans zero, so this ratio is a rough magnitude, not a measured quantity. Roughly a third of the full 4A/0D damage was avoided, i.e. about two thirds was still incurred.

POST_HOC_DESCRIPTIVE_NOT_PRE_REGISTERED.note: Everything in this block was computed AFTER seeing the gate result. None of it gates anything, none of it changes the label, and it is a small fixed set rather than an open search.

router_beats_fixed_4A0D_on_B.reading: Interval excludes zero. Time-varying composition did better on Pole B than either constant composition. Single post-hoc contrast at n=64, one block: a lead, not a finding.

harm_is_entirely_in_triggered_episodes.reading: The whole +0.172 harm sits in the 39 episodes where the router fired. The untriggered episodes contribute exactly zero, by determinism. The router fired disproportionately in episodes where fixed 2A/2D already wins 74% of the time, so it fired where there was most to lose. Unexplained; not interpreted further.

the_calibration_safety_proxy_did_not_pre.v1_spec_justification_quoted: COMPOSITION_SELECTOR_ASYMMETRIC_B_TRIGGER_V1_SPEC.json justified the 0.10 A false-positive TICK budget as: 'rough linear exposure ~0.03 win rate if harm scaled by exposure, well below that measured full switch cost.'
the_calibration_safety_proxy_did_not_pre.linear_prediction: closed-loop A tick fraction 0.1094 x full-time 4A/0D damage in this block 0.2656 = 0.029
the_calibration_safety_proxy_did_not_pre.even_at_the_calibration_tick_rate: At the held-out calibration rate of 0.0674 the linear prediction is 0.018, so the miss is not explained by the closed-loop rate being higher.
the_calibration_safety_proxy_did_not_pre.reading: Harm is strongly superlinear in tick exposure: about 43 ticks (18% of an episode) in 4A/0D inside a triggered episode cost roughly as much win rate as spending the whole episode there. The premise that a tick-level false-positive budget bounds outcome harm is contradicted. The mechanism is NOT established by this run.

open_loop_vs_closed_loop_exposure.reading: Exposure was higher on both poles once the router actually acted. This is consistent with the router's own switching changing the state it reads (calibration traces came from a fixed 2A/2D team), but it is equally consistent with sampling: 0.0674 came from 16 Pole-A episodes and its own held-out bootstrap interval was [0.031, 0.110], which contains 0.1094. This run cannot separate the two, and it does not need to for the label.

establishes: A scripted two-feature router captured a very large Pole-B gain (+0.672, LCB95 +0.516) at n=64 paired seeds, consistent across both halves.
The same router demonstrably harms Pole A (+0.172, LCB95 +0.047, UCB95 +0.297), beyond the frozen 0.10 tolerance, consistently across both halves.
The calibration-side safety criterion (a false-positive tick-rate budget) did not bound outcome-level harm.
does_not_establish: a sealed result: the record is AUDIT_FAILED
why a short 4A/0D exposure is so costly on Pole A: switching cost, timing of the trigger, and attack-heavy composition at those moments are all still open
that the harm generalizes beyond these two frozen opponents at 4v4
any claim about PPO, learned coordination, or 6v6

OPEN_DECISIONS_FOR_THE_PI_NONE_AUTHORIZE.1_seal_the_record: Fix run_state.py so the seed_class audit passes the run's own experiment_id (with a test that a Rule-9-compliant run can seal), then re-audit the persisted rows under a NEW label. No new episodes, no new seeds; the deterministic bootstrap seed means the claims should re-derive identically. Needs a go-ahead because it edits shared integrity infrastructure after the verdict is known. The original AUDIT_FAILED record stays as it is.
OPEN_DECISIONS_FOR_THE_PI_NONE_AUTHORIZE.2_no_router_retuning: Consistent with the frozen spec and with the PI's standing direction: the operating point stays frozen. A retune of the threshold or hysteresis now would be exactly the outcome-driven tuning the selector freeze was written to prevent.
OPEN_DECISIONS_FOR_THE_PI_NONE_AUTHORIZE.3_where_the_harm_comes_from: Whether the Pole-A cost comes from the switch itself, from its timing, or from the attack-heavy composition at those moments decides whether the next move is a transition fix or a different coordination mechanism. That would need its own pre-registered diagnostic on a fresh block; nothing further was run here.
